brief: BofA's Flow Show argues markets are not panicking despite the highest 30yr yield since Jun'07 and spiking commodities, and reads that calm as a setup for volatility. Oil at $100/bbl takes headlines but diesel at a $6 record is the key real-economy pressure point through shipping, trucking, agriculture, construction and mining, so a break below the 200-day moving average at 80 in transportation stocks (IYT) would turn summer macro derisking into an autumn stagflation event. A big yield surge is judged too harmful to both Main St and Wall St, with the $1tn Treasury General Account waiting. Peak yield trades are working ahead of central bank hikes, but the long-duration rally in XBI, KRE, REITs and small caps is unmatched by flows, so BofA says it is not too late to hedge AI-soaked stock indexes. The bond diversification benefit is fading as stock and bond returns correlate again, so allocators may require higher yields before buying bonds. Weekly flows: $17.5bn to bonds, $9.8bn to stocks, $3.9bn out of US equities. Bull and Bear Indicator down to 9.5, signal Sell.
